about.repoDescription: The app's open-source code on GitHub.

recovery.label: Reopen windows on launch
recovery.description: Which of the windows open when you last quit Vertex (or when it crashed) are reopened when it starts. Each comes back at its size and place, with its tabs.

language.title: Language
language.label: App language
language.description: The language of menus and the interface.

channel.label: Update channel
channel.description: The release channel Vertex updates from.
channel.loadFailed: Couldn't load channels from the update server: {error}

token.label: Channel token
token.description: Optional token for restricted channels. Stored in your system keychain.
token.saved: A token is saved in your system keychain.

theme.title: Theme
theme.previewText: Markdown, links and code use the editor fonts below.
theme.primaryDescription: Buttons, links, selection and focus rings.
theme.colorModeDescription: Light, dark, or follow the system.
theme.radiusDescription: How rounded buttons, inputs and panels are.
theme.editorMonoFontDescription: Code blocks and inline code in notes.
theme.customCssDescription: Added after Vertex's own styles. Saved when you leave the editor.
theme.customCssUntrusted: This workspace's CSS is off until you trust the workspace: it could restyle or hide anything, the trust prompt included.

view.title: View
view.statusBarDescription: Display mode of the status bar.
view.selectionToolbarDescription: Show a formatting toolbar above selected text.
view.slashMenuDescription: Type / to open a menu of blocks to insert.
view.blockHandleDescription: Show a handle beside blocks to drag or move them.
view.headerHistoryDescription: Where the header shows undo and redo.
view.headerFormattingDescription: Where the header shows bold, italic, strikethrough and highlight.
view.panelsDescription: Which views each side panel has, in what order, and how you switch between them. Rearrange them here, or by dragging or right-clicking their buttons in a window.
view.panelStyleDescription: Buttons inside the panels, or icon strips at the window’s edges (click the shown view’s icon to collapse its panel).
view.panelLayoutDescription: Drag views between the sides and Hidden; right-click one to move it, hide it or add a separator.
view.updateLinks: Update links after a move or rename
view.updateLinksDescription: When a note or folder is moved or renamed, what happens to the links that pointed to it. Ask is the default; the dialog's Remember choice sets it for a workspace.
view.deletedFilesDescription: Where Delete in Files sends items. The Trash and the workspace’s .trash folder (hidden from Files) can be undone; deleting permanently asks first and cannot be undone.
view.attachmentsFolderDescription: Where files from outside the workspace go when chat or a note takes them, and pasted screenshots. Created when first needed.
view.importToChatDescription: Files dropped or pasted into chat from Finder or Explorer are copied into the attachments folder first. Ask is the default; the dialog’s Remember choice sets it for a workspace.

trust.title: Trust
trust.trustedDescription: Programs here (workflows) run without asking, and a trusted workspace's own settings apply: its custom CSS, the plugins it turns on, its AI and git settings. Everything else asks first.
trust.noTrusted: Nothing yet. A workflow’s first run or a workspace’s settings ask you, or add a folder or file here.
trust.unreadable: “{name}” can’t be read as a program
trust.fileTrustDescription: Paths and content: a trusted file, or a trusted folder's programs as they were when you trusted it, run only while unchanged outside Vertex; edits in Vertex keep them trusted, and a program added or changed elsewhere (sync, git, another app, a workflow) asks first. Paths: anything at a trusted path runs.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.coreDescription: Built into Vertex. Turning one off removes what it adds once Vertex restarts.

reason.missing: Off: it needs {name}, which isn't installed
reason.requirementOff: Off: it needs {name}, which is off

plugins.untrusted: This workspace turns on plugins that are off in your settings. They run once you trust it.

restart.title: Restart Vertex to turn off {name}?
restart.description: It keeps running until Vertex restarts. Your workspace windows open again after the restart.

plugins.settingsWaitForTrust: Some of this workspace's changes here apply only once you trust it.

scope.label: Editing
scope.help: A workspace's own settings live in its .vertex/settings.json and override yours there.
scope.globalOnlyPage: A workspace can't change these settings; they apply everywhere.

git.title: Git
git.tokensDescription: Personal access tokens for HTTPS remotes, saved when a remote refused to sign in. They stay in your system keychain; git gets one only while it talks to its host, and your own credential helpers aren't asked then.
git.noTokens: No saved tokens. Vertex asks for one when a remote refuses to sign in.
git.failed: Couldn't read or change the saved tokens

autoSync.title: Auto-sync
autoSync.description: Keeps this computer's workspaces in step without pressing Sync: commits every change, pulls and pushes. It waits during a merge or rebase and pauses after a sign-in failure until a sync from the Git view works. A trusted workspace can have its own.
autoSync.intervalDescription: How often a workspace window syncs while it's open.
autoSync.pullOnFocus: Pull when the window gets focus
autoSync.pullOnFocusDescription: Brings in the remote's new commits when you come back to the window (at most once a minute).
autoSync.untrusted: This workspace's auto-sync applies once its folder is trusted.

ui.selectFile: Select a file from the left side.

filetree.newFileDescription: Creates a new Markdown file in the workspace root.
filetree.newFolderDescription: Creates a new folder in the workspace root.
filetree.importFailed: Could not add the dropped items.
filetree.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard.
filetree.nothingToPaste: The clipboard has no files to paste.
filetree.trashedWorkspace: Moved {count} item(s) to the workspace’s .trash folder.
filetree.undoSkipped: Some items were left as they are, since they changed or moved after that step: {names}
filetree.redoSkipped: Some items were left as they are, since they changed or moved after the undo: {names}
filetree.undoNotLast: Something changed in Files since. Press Cmd/Ctrl+Z in Files to undo the latest change first.

updateLinks.title: Update links to “{name}”?
updateLinks.description: {links} link(s) in {files} note(s) point to the old name or place.
updateLinks.remember: Remember my decision for this workspace

conflict.title: “{name}” already exists in {folder}
conflict.description: Replace the existing item, keep both (the new one gets a number), or skip this one.
conflict.applyToAll: Do this for the remaining {count} conflict(s)

ui.blockHandle: Drag to move block, click for options

ai.stale: The text changed since this was generated. Retry to use the current text.
ai.staleTool: The text changed since this was suggested.

aiFeatures.editorAssistantDescription: Ask AI in the editor: rewrite, fix, continue and more.
aiFeatures.chatDescription: Chats about your notes. A chat can pin its own profile. Off hides the Chats and Chat views, Ask in chat and New Chat.
aiFeatures.commitMessageDescription: Writes commit messages from the changes, in the style of the repository's recent ones: the Git view's sparkle button, and when you set it below, an empty message box and auto-sync. The diff is sent to the model.

chat.placeholder: Ask anything about your notes… Type {'@'} to attach one
chat.title: Title
chat.deleteFolderConfirm: "{folder}", its subfolders and every chat in them will be deleted for good.
chat.noModel: Chat is off or has no model. Choose one in Settings → AI Features.

vault.createDescription: This workspace's chats are encrypted inside its folder.
vault.noRecovery: There's no way to recover a forgotten password: without it, these chats can't be read.

toolsUnsupported.title: This model can't use tools
toolsUnsupported.description: {model} doesn't support tool calling, so the request was stopped. Turn tools off for this model profile and try again? You can turn them back on in the profile's settings.

tools.waiting: waiting for you in the note

rewind.title: Rewind to this reply?
rewind.description: The {count} message(s) after it will be removed, with their branches.
rewind.undo: It also undoes the changes applied from those replies: {paths}
rewind.skipped: Left {count} note(s) as they are: they changed since

context.title: Context: {title}
context.totals: {messages} messages · {calls} model calls · {input} tokens in · {output} out · {seconds} s
context.notRecorded: Not recorded: this reply is from before Vertex kept its context.

changes.title: Changes ({count})
changes.conflicts: {count} change(s) not applied: the note changed after it was staged

states.conflict: Not applied: the note changed after it was staged

changes.gone: This change isn't in the chat any more.
changes.chatFailed: Couldn't open the chat this change belongs to.
changes.conflictNote: The note changed after this was staged; this is what the AI proposed against the text it read.

waitingPlaceholder.question: Answer the question above, or type your answer here…
waitingPlaceholder.approval: Type here to decline, and say why…

attach.tooBig: Over 5 MB, too big to send: {names}

importDialog.title: Add {count} file(s) to the workspace?
importDialog.description: Chat attaches workspace files, so they’re copied into {folder} first.

chat.imagesUnsupported: The model {model} doesn’t take images. Remove the attached images or choose a model that does.

panels.mergeLeft: Merge with the pane on the left

git.label: Git
git.syncHint: Commit every change, pull the remote's new commits, then push yours.
git.fetch: Fetch: check the remote for new commits
git.pull: Pull: bring in the remote's new commits
git.push: Push: send your commits to the remote
git.branchPlaceholder: Switch to or create a branch…
git.stagedHint: Staged changes go into the next commit.
git.changesHint: Changes not staged yet. Stage them to put them in the next commit.

discardConfirm.title: Discard changes?
discardConfirm.description: {count} file(s) go back to how they were in the last commit, and new files are deleted. This can't be undone.

git.commitHint: Save the staged changes as a commit: a snapshot in the history.
git.commitAllHint: Nothing is staged, so this commits every change.
git.commitPushHint: Commit, then send it to the remote.

merging.title: Merging
merging.description: Resolve each conflict: keep yours (this device's) or theirs (the remote's), or fix the file and mark it resolved. Then finish the merge, or abort to go back.

missing.title: Git isn't installed
missing.description: Vertex uses git to track and sync this workspace. Install it, then check again.
missing.macos: Vertex uses git to track and sync this workspace. Apple's developer tools include it: install them, then check again.
missing.configured: Vertex is set to use {path}, which isn't a working git. Locate another, or let Vertex find one.
missing.toolsFailed: Couldn't open the developer tools installer

notRepo.title: Not a git repository
notRepo.description: This workspace isn't tracked by git yet. Creating a repository starts tracking its changes, with a .gitignore that leaves out system files and Vertex's trash.

notRepo.title: Not a git repository
notRepo.description: This workspace isn't tracked by git.

auth.title: Couldn't sign in to the remote
auth.description: The remote refused to sign in. For an HTTPS remote, try again and enter a personal access token; for SSH, add your key to the SSH agent.

conflict.title: Merge conflicts
conflict.description: Some files changed both here and on the remote. Resolve them in the Git view's Conflicts list, then finish the merge, or abort it.

rejected.title: The remote has newer commits
rejected.description: Pull them in first, then push again.

noRemote.title: No remote to sync with
noRemote.description: This repository isn't connected to a remote yet: connect one to push.

noUpstream.title: This branch has no remote branch
noUpstream.description: It doesn't track a branch on a remote, and there's no `origin` to push it to. Push it once with `git push -u` and the remote's name.

identity.title: Git needs your name and email
identity.description: Commits record who made them. Set your name and email to commit.

git.syncChatsHint: Chats kept in this workspace are encrypted files git can't merge: when two devices change the same chat, you pick one version.

diff.againstParent: Compared with the commit before it

history.label: History
history.show: History: every commit, as a graph
history.emptyHint: Commit your changes to start the history.

signIn.title: Sign in to {host}
signIn.description: Git couldn't sign in to {host}. A personal access token lets it.
signIn.refused: {host} refused the saved token. It may have expired or lost access: enter a new one.
signIn.explain: A personal access token is a password for apps, made in your account settings on the host. Give it read and write access to your repositories.
signIn.createElsewhere: Create one in your account settings on {host}.
signIn.usernameHelp: Only if your host wants your username with tokens.
signIn.kept: Vertex keeps it in your system keychain and hands it to git only while it talks to {host}. Remove it in Settings → Git.

identity.title: Your name and email
identity.description: Every commit records who made it. These are kept in this repository only.
identity.name: Name

remote.title: Connect a remote
remote.description: A remote is a copy of this repository on a server, like GitHub. Your devices sync through it: each pushes its commits there and pulls the others'.
remote.empty: Make it private, and leave it empty: no README, .gitignore or license, so the first push goes straight in. Then copy its HTTPS URL here.

push.title: Push your notes
push.description: Vertex commits every file and pushes the commit to the remote. If the remote asks you to sign in, Vertex helps you make a token.

sync.title: Sync
sync.description: One click keeps your devices in step: it commits every change, pulls the remote's new commits, then pushes yours.

branch.title: Branch
branch.description: A branch is a line of work. Switch branches here, or type a name to start a new one.

aheadBehind.title: Ahead and behind
aheadBehind.description: Commits of yours the remote doesn't have yet (up arrow), and commits on the remote you haven't pulled (down arrow).

remoteActions.title: Fetch, pull and push
remoteActions.description: Fetch checks the remote for new commits, pull brings them into your files, push sends your commits to the remote.

list.title: Changes and staged
list.description: Changes lists the files you edited since the last commit. Stage (plus) the ones that go into the next commit: they move to Staged. Click a file to see what changed.

commit.title: Commit
commit.description: A commit saves the staged changes (or every change, when nothing is staged) as one step in the history, with a message saying what changed.

history.title: History
history.description: Every commit, branch by branch: select one to see what it changed.

clone.title: Clone a workspace
clone.description: Copy a repository from a remote into a new folder and open it as a workspace.
clone.name: Folder name

conflicts.label: Conflicts
conflicts.hint: Files changed both here and on the remote. Keep one side, or open the file, fix the parts git marked and mark it resolved.
conflicts.markersConfirm: {count} file(s) still have conflict markers: {files}. Mark them resolved anyway?

rebasing.title: Rebasing
rebasing.description: Your commits are being replayed onto the remote's. Resolve each conflict: keep yours (this device's) or theirs (the remote's), or fix the file and mark it resolved. Then continue; a later commit may stop again. Or abort to go back.

diff.binaryHint: It has no lines to compare.
